subject: Follow-up: Redwood Private VPC — networking, control plane & air-gap feasibility
messages:

Cc: AcmeHealth Security <sec-team@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-15T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Redwood Private VPC - networking & air-gap feasibility

Hi Sarah - thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we can scope the technical workshop: 

Key takeaways from the call:
- Primary goal: run Redwood Private in AcmeHealth VPC with an option for an air-gapped/on-prem install for PHI workloads.
- Concerns called out: egress control (no internet egress for some workloads), control plane placement and telemetry, KMS/HSM integration, and SOC2 evidence.
- Competitor note: you mentioned your team is also evaluating hyperscaler-managed inference (AWS PrivateLink + managed endpoints) and a couple of inference APIs.

Proposed next tests we suggested on the call:
1) Networking test: share a test VPC (CIDRs, subnets, routing) so we can validate peering/PrivateLink-style connectivity and NAT behavior.
2) Control plane validation: demo hosted control plane vs local control plane options and show how control traffic is isolated.
3) Air-gap feasibility: walkthrough the on-prem package requirements (ports, images, bootstrap steps) and identify any blocked egress.
4) Security artifacts: share SOC2 attestation + KMS integration plan.

Attachments: redwood-private-deployment-overview.pdf, initial-mrp-checklist.xlsx (high-level runbook and checklist).

Ask: Can you share the test VPC details (CIDRs, route tables, NAT/bastion details) and a list of stakeholders for a 90-minute technical workshop? Camila (CC'd) from our infra team will lead the session. Suggested dates: Oct 20 or Oct 22.

Thanks - I’ll prep a focused runbook and competitor brief ahead of the call.

Best,

Thanks Sarah - great to meet you both. A few technical clarifications and an initial networking test plan so we can hit the ground running during the workshop. I'm pasting the plan below and attaching the more detailed test plan and control plane options doc.

Quick technical notes (short answers):
- Control plane: two options - (1) Redwood hosted control plane with encrypted control channel to your VPC (minimal outbound to Redwood endpoints) or (2) Local control plane (customer-owned) where control plane components run in your VPC/on-prem. For fully air-gapped workloads we recommend the local control plane option.
- KMS/HSM: we support BYOK via KMS integrations; for air-gapped/on-prem we can integrate with on-prem HSMs via our key proxy.
- Egress: air-gapped configuration requires blocked egress from worker subnets; bootstrap requires a one-time image transfer or an internal mirror of our packages.

Initial networking test plan (high level):
1) Validate VPC peering / PrivateLink behavior by deploying a small test instance in your test subnet and verifying TCP connectivity to Redwood worker IPs.
2) Validate NAT behavior: confirm whether outbound to S3 or package registries is allowed from worker subnets; if not, plan for an internal mirror.
3) DNS + service discovery: ensure internal DNS resolution for control-plane endpoints (if using local control plane) or allow our control endpoints via an allowlist.
4) IAM/KMS validation: we will do a KMS encrypt/decrypt handshake using your test key.

Attachments: private-control-plane-options.pdf, networking-test-plan.md

Can you share a small set of test IPs, route tables, and the NAT/bastion details? We can then finalize the workshop agenda (proposed: 90 minutes - 45m networking + controls, 45m hands-on).

Cheers,
Camila Reyes
Staff Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com
